title: Data for semilinear transport of sheaf tensor presentations
statement: For sites small in a common value universe [def-weil-size-convention], use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A tensor presentation of a fixed ring map D → A is a sheaf B, a map D → B, a sheaf R and maps A → R, B → R forming a pushout in commutative-ring sheaves; equivalently it is an isomorphism A ⊗_D B ≅ R, recorded by its inclusions. For an inverse-image functor F of a geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], compatible presentation transport consists of ring isomorphisms d,a,b,c on the inverse-image underlying sheaves, preserving all ring-operation graphs on every test sheaf, and commuting with the two D-structure maps and both presentation inclusions. Define additive and semilinear transport by preservation of their addition and scalar-action graphs on every test sheaf. For an A-module M, use the existing sheafified tensor N=M ⊗_D B and its actual pure pairing. The presentation action predicate on sectionwise R-module structures on N requires semilinear restrictions and (i_A(x)i_B(v)) · (m ⊗ w) = (x · m) ⊗ (vw). For an adjunction F ⊣ V, the adjunct-normalization predicate on r:FN_Y ≅ N_X is the equality of maps out of M_Y × B_Y between its actual adjunct after the pure pairing and V of the target pairing after the actual adjuncts of s,b, using the inverse canonical product comparison of the right adjoint V. A coefficient change consists of D-algebra maps q:B → B′ and ring maps i:R → R′ commuting with both presentation inclusions. Its additive tensor map is characterized by m ⊗ v ↦ m ⊗ q(v). Underlying-set, underlying-abelian-sheaf and restriction-of-scalars views are the existing forgetful functors; no additional module structures or maps are chosen.
